correction: Distinguish the share of harmed animals from the share of attack events. The primary report’s2024figures2and3give respectively91%of4300harmed animals and79%of1109attacks for sheep/goats. One attack can harm multiple animals. The oral statement does not name a year or local source; identification of the91%as this statistic is a strong matching inference, not an explicit citation.
effect: Reduces the matched2024attack-event share by approximately12percentage points, weakening the stated concentration of attack events on the represented livestock sector. Sheep and goats nevertheless remain by far the largest affected category under both measures.
limits: An oral shorthand use of attacks to mean harms is plausible. The91%animal share is valid and still supports a serious burden. The record does not determine the actual2025or2026event share, the effectiveness of herd protection, an individual keeper’s loss or whether the proposed removals are appropriate. The report includes killed, injured and missing animals and differing state attribution criteria; it is not simply a confirmed-kills census. No intent is inferred.
context_and_alternatives: Read the full four-page writtenVDLsubmission and opening oral statement physical9–10, plus relevant question-answer context physical11,13,20–21. The written statement explicitly cites dated2023counts, which are not treated as current or fabricated. The opening oral statement is the distinct source for this finding. No full28-page transcript review is claimed.

Strongest benign explanation: colloquial substitution of attacks for animals affected in a short oral statement. This limits severity; the official report expressly distinguishes both quantities on the same page.

The oral statement gives no year. The latest matching2024report was publishedJuly2025before theFebruary2026hearing. Identification rests on the exact91%and sheep/goat pairing, strengthened by the speaker’s later explicitDBBW2024reference for protection expenditure. No source copying or intent is alleged.

The companion claim that losses are increasing could refer to the long run or hotspots despite the2024national decline; it is not promoted as a separate falsehood. Policy forecasts and practical experiences in the later answers are not disproved by the denominator correction.
materiality_explanation: Minor: the event-share description overstates the matching figure, but correcting it leaves a clear majority of attacks on sheep/goats and preserves the central claim of disproportionate burden. The numerical difference alone does not make the overall policy argument fail.
direction_explanation: True narrowly: a larger apparent share of attack events strengthens the represented sector’s argument for urgent removal and management measures. This does not establish intent or the merits of the request.
